rule: Reviewer fix-cycle commits are sanctioned, never forbidden
description: Commit/push authority is a structural POSITIVE GRANT ALLOWLIST in safety-rails.md's Commit Authority subsection (COMMIT-GRANT marker lines for orchestrator, local-reviewer, github-reviewer, synapse, delegated-implementer). set_check asserts the grant SET itself (equal mode + expected_counts) so a deleted grant, an unreviewed extra grant, or a duplicated grant all fail structurally instead of requiring one more literal clause pin per review pass. SCOPE BOUNDARY (deliberate, not an oversight): this assertion pins WHO HOLDS AUTHORITY AT ALL — the grant-set membership — and does NOT pin each grant's condition prose (entry points, standing vs delegation-scoped, push count, PR-mutation negatives). Pinning those dimensions one at a time is the literal-enumeration treadmill this fixture was rewritten to end: each added dimension leaves the next un-pinned dimension as the next review finding, so it never closes the class. The condition prose stays human-reviewed; the machine check owns the membership axis, where silent privilege expansion actually lives. The extraction is anchored on the COMMIT-GRANT MARKER rather than on a key charset so no authored grant line can be invisible to the check: any key that is not in expected_set surfaces as an extra and fails equal mode, including keys a charset-constrained capture would have skipped past (uppercase, digits, underscores). The `<` exclusion keeps the fixed-form template line (`COMMIT-GRANT <key>: ...`) out of the captured set; any other COMMIT-GRANT occurrence in the file is captured and must reconcile against the expected set. The remaining consumers entries are a bounded tail: the source-of-truth sentence, one citation-anchor pin per referencing agent doc, and the small set of step-mechanics clauses that are not expressible as a grant-set member. Two consumers bear on the synapse grant. In plugin/agents/synapse.md the sentence saying the runner needs no grant in the prompt and no message from the user, and so never reports blocked for want of one, is pinned; deleting or rewording it is loud. In plugin/governance/safety-rails.md the start of the delegated-implementer grant line, naming drone and changeling as its committers, is pinned; rewording that start is loud, but the pin covers only that word sequence, so synapse added later in the same line leaves it green. This fixture does not check that synapse is absent from the delegated-implementer line: the standard-delivery workflow node test (row SD-74 in tests/workflow-scripts/standard-delivery.test.mjs) asserts the whole line does not include synapse. What these two pins do not check: they claim word sequences only, never meaning, so a rewrite elsewhere in either file that contradicts them is unseen; they cannot see that synapse.md's body carries no per-prompt grant check (body absence is beyond a presence pin, and the standard-delivery workflow node test checks that instead); and the synapse grant line's own condition prose (the runner commands it covers, its gate bound, its trunk negative) stays human-reviewed like every other grant's condition prose.

source.pattern: Commit and push authority is a POSITIVE GRANT

consumers.pattern: EXPLICITLY forbids this agent from committing
Absence of commit-policy language is not a prohibition
This checkpoint is load-bearing for convergence
MUST SANCTION the reviewer's own fix-cycle checkpoint commits
MUST NOT forbid the reviewer committing
this prohibition is scoped to WAVE WORKER delegations
It needs no grant in the prompt and no message from the user, so never report `blocked` for want of one.
`COMMIT-GRANT delegated-implementer:` drone and changeling commit or push ONLY when their delegation explicitly authorizes it
